newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW - Mondragon sees 430 mln pesos net.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Mondragon sees 430 mln pesos net.

text.p: Mondragon International Philippines Inc chairman and chief executive officer Jose Antonio Gonzalez said on Wednesday his firm's net income may reach 430 million pesos in 1996.
"We are on target with our income projections. At this point, our net income figure is slightly ahead of our earlier full-year 425 million-peso forecast," Gonzalez told Reuters.
"We may reach a 430-million peso net income by year end," Gonzalez added.
Mondragon posted a net income of 212.17 million pesos in 1995.
Brokers said the opening of the firm's Mimosa casino at the Clark economic zone in the northern Philippines on September 27 would boost the firm's profits.
"We expect the casino to bring a net income of 450 million pesos in its first 12 months of operations," Gonzalez said.

Mondragon shares lost 75 centavos to 14.75 pesos on the Philippine Stock Exchange on Wednesday on market rumours that its casino earnings were lower than expected in its first few weeks of operations.

"Earnings concerns, such as talk that Mondragon's casino may not be able to meet its initial earnings target in its first month of operation due to the absence of the high rollers, dampened interest on the issue," one broker told Reuters.
Gonzalez shrugged off the rumours as an "old wives' tale".
"You cannot open a restaurant and expect it to be jampacked every day," he said.
"We're delighted with the public response to the casino. We don't expect though to make tons of money right away," Gonzalez said.
"But we are making money at the casino," he added.
Gonzalez said his firm expects business to pick up at the casino as it establishes its market.
"We expect to triple the business we are doing at the casino right now as we are starting to attract regulars," he added.
Henry Ong, analyst at Sapphire Securities, said he had downgraded Mondragon's earnings forecast for 1996 to 320 million pesos from the 425 million previously.
"The casino is finally open but the crowd was not there to co-operate," Sapphire analyst Kevin Khoe said in an advisory to clients. --Manila newsroom (632) 841-89-36, fax 817-62-67
